macros.name: horoadjcycles
macros.doc: a hard limit on how many cycles of adjustment the system will do, set by \horoadjcycles.

macros.name: horoadjust
macros.doc: The ready-made templates will invoke \horoadjust automatically at the right time to adjust the locations of objects, but it can also be invoked manually in the context of user-created templates.

macros.name: horoanglearrowstrue
macros.doc: Angular cusps can also be highlighted by giving them arrowheads; this is selected with \horoanglearrowstrue and \horoanglearrowsfalse, default true.

macros.name: horoanglecuspwidth
macros.doc: Line width to use in drawing angular cusps when \horoboldangles is turned on.

macros.name: horoaspectobjectsa
macros.doc: List of objects that can appear on one side of an aspect relation.

macros.name: horoaspectobjectsb
macros.doc: List of objects that can appear on the other side of an aspect relation.

macros.name: horoaspects
macros.doc: The \horoaspects macro stores a list of aspects to include in aspect webs, much in the manner that \horoobjects lists objects to include in charts.

macros.name: horoastrologopt
macros.doc: The macros \horoastrologopt and \horosweopt define extra command-line options for the external calculation programs (Astrolog and swetest respectively).

macros.name: horoautoaspect
macros.doc: To automatically find and draw aspects of a given type, use \horoautoaspect{hlist1i}{hlist2i}{⟨angle⟩}{⟨orb⟩}{⟨radius⟩}{⟨symbol⟩}. This searches for all pairs of one object from hlist1i with one object from hlist2i whose Pos values are ⟨angle⟩◦ apart (in either direction) to within ⟨orb⟩◦ .

macros.name: horoautoaspects
macros.doc: \horoautoaspects{⟨radius⟩} (note plural) draws a complete aspect web of the kind demonstrated by the default templates.

macros.name: horoboldanglesfalse
macros.doc: With \horoboldanglestrue and \horoboldanglesfalse the user can select whether to display angular house cusps as extra-bold lines.

macros.name: horoboldanglestrue
macros.doc: With \horoboldanglestrue and \horoboldanglesfalse the user can select whether to display angular house cusps as extra-bold lines.

macros.name: horocalcharmonic
macros.doc: The \horocalcharmonic{⟨harmonic⟩} macro multiplies all the Pos values of objects in \horoobjects by its argument and sets the Pos and DPos values to the result.

macros.name: horocalculate
macros.doc: call \horocalculate to invoke the external calculation program and actually compute the object positions.

macros.name: horochoosetextsize
macros.doc: This makes some attempt to choose a reasonable text size based on \horolbllen, so that labels with more chunks will be set in smaller type.

macros.name: horocopyvar
macros.doc: The \horocopyvar{⟨objects⟩}{⟨from⟩}{⟨to⟩} macro copies the ⟨from⟩ variable to the ⟨to⟩ variable on all the objects in the comma-separated list given by ⟨objects⟩.

macros.name: horocuspadjusttrigger
macros.doc: This represents the percentage of the normal “minimum” distance between objects and objects, or objects and cusps, below which houses will be considered too cramped.

macros.name: horocusps
macros.doc: The macro \horocusps lists the cusps, like \horoobjects, but in general it should not be modified.

macros.name: horodsmstext
macros.doc: The \horodsmstext macro prints its argument as an astrological longitude with degree, (Zodiac) sign, minutes, and seconds.

macros.name: horoforeach
macros.doc: To run a macro on every object in a comma-separated list, call \horoforeach{⟨list⟩}{⟨macro⟩}.

macros.name: horohouselabel
macros.doc: Each house label results in a call to \horohouselabel, which by default typesets the horohouse LaTeX counter in uppercase Roman numerals.

macros.name: horointhouselabelsfalse
macros.doc: Internal house labels are numbers that appear inside the houses among the object labels, selected with the \horointhouselabelstrue and \horointhouselabelsfalse macros.

macros.name: horointhouselabelstrue
macros.doc: Internal house labels are numbers that appear inside the houses among the object labels, selected with the \horointhouselabelstrue and \horointhouselabelsfalse macros.

macros.name: horolatlontext
macros.doc: Typesets the first argument as a number of degrees, minutes, and seconds, with the second and third arguments added at the end for positive or negative respectively.

macros.name: horomakeequalcusps
macros.doc: Use \horomakeequalcusps to make twelve cusps spaced equally (30◦ apart) with CuspI set to the single argument.

macros.name: horomakesigncusps
macros.doc: A similar macro, \horomakesigncusps, makes equally-spaced cusps just like \horomakeequalcusps (in fact, using a call to it) but starting from the start of the sign that contains the argument value instead of starting at the argument value itself.

macros.name: horomarvosym
macros.doc: The macros \horotextsym, \horounicode, \horowasysym, \horomarvosym, and \horostarfont switch to the corresponding set of astrological symbols, so that documents can mix the different sets.

macros.name: horomaxrepulsion
macros.doc: Interference distance (in degrees) at which maximum repulsion is achieved.

macros.name: horominutes
macros.doc: Symbols for degrees, minutes, and seconds (\horodegrees, \horominutes, and \horoseconds) are provided for use when an angle will be described numerically, as in 12◦ 340 5600 .

macros.name: horoobjects
macros.doc: Calculation and the chart templates use a macro called \horoobjects, which lists the names (comma separated) of all the objects to compute or typeset.

macros.name: horoocmindist
macros.doc: Object/cusp minimum distance.

macros.name: horooomindist
macros.doc: Object/object minimum distance.

macros.name: horoposattcusp
macros.doc: Strength of attraction between a cusp and its desired Pos value.

macros.name: horoposattobj
macros.doc: Strength of attraction between an object and its desired Pos value.

macros.name: horoputarrowhead
macros.doc: Draw an arrowhead with its tip at (r = #1, θ = #2), pointing outward from the origin.

macros.name: horoputarrows
macros.doc: It places arrowheads (not actually complete arrows) pointing outward with their tips on the circle of radius ⟨r⟩.

macros.name: horoputcusplabel
macros.doc: The \horoputcusplabel{⟨radius⟩}{⟨spacing⟩}{⟨object⟩} macro draws a style of label designed to show the longitude of an angle or cusp.

macros.name: horoputinthouselabels
macros.doc: Use \horoputinthouselabels{⟨radius⟩} to draw a set of internal house labels.

macros.name: horoputobjdeglabel
macros.doc: Typeset a label consisting of the object’s degree and sign.

macros.name: horoputobjseclabel
macros.doc: Typesets a four-chunk label reading degrees, sign, minutes, seconds.

macros.name: horoputobjsymbol
macros.doc: Put the symbol for object #2 at its DPos and radius #1.

macros.name: horoputradial
macros.doc: The \horoputradial{⟨radius⟩}{⟨length⟩}{⟨theta⟩} macro draws a radial line out from the point at radius ⟨radius⟩ and longitude ⟨theta⟩ for a length of ⟨length⟩.

macros.name: horoputradials
macros.doc: Iterate through a list of objects drawing radials for each. Normally you’d use this to draw the radial lines separating houses.

macros.name: horoputrxlabel
macros.doc: The \horoputrxlabel{⟨radius⟩}{⟨object⟩} macro typesets an optional retrograde label for the object at the object’s DPos and radius ⟨radius⟩: if the object’s Vel is negative then the label will appear as the value of \horoRetrogradeSymbol and otherwise it will be blank.

macros.name: horoputsignkey
macros.doc: The \horoputsignkey{⟨r⟩} macro creates a sign key, which consists of all twelve Zodiac sign symbols, each placed with its centre at radius ⟨r⟩ and longitude 15◦ into its own sign.

macros.name: horoputsmartlabel
macros.doc: The \horoputsmartlabel{⟨object⟩} macro provides elaborately-configurable labels as seen in the Vancouver template.

macros.name: hororepulsion
macros.doc: Basic divisor for repulsion between all pairs of things that are repelled from each other.

macros.name: hororotatechart
macros.doc: the \hororotatechart{⟨object⟩}{⟨angle⟩} macro will rotate a chart to place a specified object at a specified place.

macros.name: hororoundautofalse
macros.doc: When \hororoundautofalse is active, the user must choose rounding modes manually.

macros.name: hororxtext
macros.doc: Typeset a “retrograde” symbol if the specified object is retrograde, determined by whether its Vel is negative.

macros.name: horosaveobjects
macros.doc: The effect is that \horosaveobjects creates a macro representing the object-related results of the last \horocalculate, so we can return to the current state later.

macros.name: horoscanlabels
macros.doc: User interface to set up \horo@lblone and \horo@lbltwo.

macros.name: horosetsmartradii
macros.doc: Sets up the radii for \horoputsmartlabel in a semi-intelligent way, sensitive to the label format string length from the previous macro.

macros.name: horoshiftcusps
macros.doc: The macros \horoshiftobjects and \horoshiftcusps apply an additive shift, specified in decimal degrees as the single argument, to all the object or cusp Pos values respectively, and sets the Pos and DPos values to the results.

macros.name: horoshiftobjects
macros.doc: The macros \horoshiftobjects and \horoshiftcusps apply an additive shift, specified in decimal degrees as the single argument, to all the object or cusp Pos values respectively, and sets the Pos and DPos values to the results.

macros.name: horosignificantadj
macros.doc: Number of degrees of adjustment that will be considered “significant” and cause another iteration.

macros.name: horostarfont
macros.doc: The macros \horotextsym, \horounicode, \horowasysym, \horomarvosym, and \horostarfont switch to the corresponding set of astrological symbols, so that documents can mix the different sets.

macros.name: horosweopt
macros.doc: The macros \horoastrologopt and \horosweopt define extra command-line options for the external calculation programs (Astrolog and swetest respectively).

macros.name: horotextsize
macros.doc: Adjustment to automatically-determined label text size in charts like Vancouver, where the text size depends on the length of the smart-label format string.

macros.name: horotextsym
macros.doc: The macros \horotextsym, \horounicode, \horowasysym, \horomarvosym, and \horostarfont switch to the corresponding set of astrological symbols, so that documents can mix the different sets.

macros.name: horounicode
macros.doc: The macros \horotextsym, \horounicode, \horowasysym, \horomarvosym, and \horostarfont switch to the corresponding set of astrological symbols, so that documents can mix the different sets.

macros.name: horounitlength
macros.doc: The unit length is set to \horounitlength, which defaults to 0.00952 times \textwidth, so that a horoscope environment will be just slightly less than the full text width of the page.

macros.name: horowheelIgloolik
macros.doc: The \horowheelIgloolik command creates a double dial, as shown in Figure 8.

macros.name: horowheelMontreal
macros.doc: The \horowheelMontreal macro generates a chart like that shown in Figure 11.

macros.name: horowheelRankin
macros.doc: Quadruple dial, radii 22, 29, 36, and 43. Optional first argument is harmonic; remaining arguments are sets of saved object positions for the dials ordered from inner to outer.

macros.name: horowheelResolute
macros.doc: Triple dial, radii 29, 36, and 43. Optional first argument is harmonic; remaining arguments are sets of saved object positions for the dials ordered from inner to outer.

macros.name: Zodiac
macros.doc: The system provides a \Zodiac{⟨sign⟩} macro, whose parameter ⟨sign⟩ should be an integer from 1 to 12 choosing the sign from Aries=1 to Pisces=12; this typesets the symbol for the appropriate sign.
